title: Urban Institute: Nonprofit-Government Contracts and Grants: Findings from the 2013 National Survey

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: Urban Institute (Pettijohn and Boris, with De Vita and coauthors)
source_type: Research report on a national, stratified random survey
reliability: Non-profit research institute report of its own survey; publication date not extracted from the document text.
findings: The survey is a national, stratified, random survey of most types of charitable nonprofits reporting $100,000 or more in expenses on IRS Form 990 in 2010.

Urban estimates government agencies entered into about 350,000 contracts and grants with about 56,000 nonprofits; the average is six per nonprofit (median three); governments paid $137 billion to nonprofits for services in 2012.
For 53 percent of respondents, late payments for services already provided were a problem; nearly 50 percent of human service nonprofits reported a late-payment problem in both 2009 and 2012.
For about 75 percent of respondents, the complexity and time required for applying and reporting on contracts and grants was a problem.
Nonprofits that said late payments were problematic were significantly more likely to draw on reserves, increase lines of credit, reduce the number of programs, and close program offices or sites.
Only 17 percent of nonprofits with budgets of $100,000 to $249,999 have a government contract or grant.
limitations: Data concern 2012; current conditions may differ substantially.
Survey excludes nonprofits under $100,000 in expenses.
Self-reported problems; no dollar cost of administrative effort was extracted.
Publication date not extracted (report on 2013 survey).
